sum: Four days north of Pokhara: a steep climb from Ghachowk through forest to Hile Kharka and the open ridge of Khumai Danda at 3,245 m, with basic lodges and Machhapuchhre close by.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this ridge a guide matters for two plain reasons: the lodges have only a few beds and need a phone call ahead, and the path above Chichemle is narrow, grassy and easy to lose in cloud or snow.

access: Ghachowk is an hour to an hour and a half north of Pokhara by taxi or jeep, on a road through Hemja, and a little longer by local bus. The trek returns to the same village. Above the Seti Khola there is no road, so once you start climbing there is no riding out part-way.

photo.a: Early sunlight catches a grassy ridge with a few small blue-roofed huts on its crest, below the sharp snow peak of Machhapuchhre and other peaks of the Annapurna range under a clear sky.
photo.c: Khumai Danda at dawn, below Machhapuchhre

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways
transportExtra: the taxi or jeep between Pokhara and Ghachowk, each way
tips: Go midweek. At weekends and on public holidays the few rooms on the ridge are taken by walkers from Pokhara.
Have your guide phone each lodge the day before. Outside the main seasons some close without notice.
Bring a warm sleeping bag, a head torch and a power bank. Rooms are unheated, blankets are few and there may be nowhere to charge a phone.
Carry two litres of water from Hile Kharka, and tablets or a filter for more.
Take the descent over two days, as planned here. Going from the top to the road in one day is a drop of 2,000 m.

days.t: Drive to Ghachowk, walk to Hile Kharka
days.note: An hour or so by road, then across the Seti Khola by footbridge and straight into the climb: about 900 m up through terraced fields and the hamlet of Tubu, then forest. It is steep for most of the way, with little shade low down. Hile Kharka is a clearing with a few plain lodges. Be walking by ten.

Up the spur through rhododendron forest to the lodge at Chichemle, then on steeper, narrower ground until the trees thin to scrub and grass below the top. You gain about 1,100 m and sleep at 3,245 m, so go slowly and drink often. Cloud usually comes in by midday; the view is for the evening and the dawn.
why: A climb of 1,085 m in one day, to sleep at 3,245 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.t: Dawn on the ridge, down to Hile Kharka
days.note: Watch the sun come up on Machhapuchhre from the ridge above the lodges. Strong walkers leave two hours before dawn for Korchon, the 3,682 m shoulder further up, and are back for a late breakfast; that adds four to five hours and is not needed for the view. Then go down the way you came.

days.t: Hile Kharka to Ghachowk, drive to Pokhara
days.note: A steep 900 m descent through forest and terraces to the bridge over the Seti Khola, hard on the knees and slippery after rain. Have lunch in Ghachowk, then take a jeep, a taxi or the local bus back to Pokhara, an hour to an hour and a half away.
